title: UniPath: Adaptive Coordination of Understanding and Generation for Unified Multimodal Reasoning
claim: Different inputs favor different reasoning strategies, so no fixed strategy is best and an oracle that picks per input far outperforms any single one.
layout: 3 panels: example cards left, accuracy heatmap top-right, instance strip below
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), on the left, shows four tall rounded cards. Each card holds one question: counting apples, the season in a snowy village, a geometry problem, and identifying an animal. Each question is solved along a different path. The paths are direct answering, understanding then reasoning, intermediate visual thought with a sketch, and multiple hypothesis thoughts. Small icons and colored section headers mark the steps, and each card ends in an answer. Panel (b), top right, is a blue-to-yellow heatmap of accuracy. Rows are five paths plus an Oracle row. Columns are MMMU subjects. Cells are outlined and dotted to mark the best path for each subject, and the Oracle row is the darkest. Panel (c), bottom right, is a barcode-style strip chart. Each row is a path, and colored ticks mark the instances that path answers correctly. The ticks show little overlap between paths.
caption: Coordination-path diversity in unified multimodal models. Different coordination paths exhibit complementary strengths across inputs. The large oracle gap over fixed strategies suggests that exploiting coordination-path diversity can significantly improve UMM performance.
abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) aim to integrate understanding and generation within a single architecture. However, it remains underexplored how to effectively coordinate these two capabilities for more effective and efficient reasoning. Existing coordination approaches either perform coupling during training, without explicit inference-time coordination, or impose a fixed coordination pattern for all inputs. In this work, we show that multimodal tasks exhibit substantial coordination-path diversity: different inputs favor different coordination paths. This suggests that exploiting such diversity is key to improving performance. We propose UniPath, a framework for adaptively modeling and exploiting coordination-path diversity. Instead of enforcing a single coordination pattern, we represent task solving as the selection and execution of a path, ranging from direct answering to textual inference, visual-thought construction, and hypothesis-based exploration. We construct role-aligned trajectories to train a path-conditioned executor and introduce a lightweight planner mechanism to enable input-dependent path selection. Experiments show that leveraging coordination-path diversity improves performance over fixed coordination strategies while providing interpretable intermediate behaviors. The code is available at:https://github.com/AIFrontierLab/TorchUMM.
